name: Austria (since 1918)
summary: The small republic left after Austria-Hungary collapsed in 1918: annexed by Nazi Germany (1938–45), occupied by the Allies until 1955, then neutral and prosperous.

knownFor.label: Vienna State Opera
knownFor.note: One of the world’s great opera houses.

knownFor.label: Sigmund Freud
knownFor.note: Founder of psychoanalysis, who worked in Vienna until 1938.

location.value: Central Europe, landlocked, mostly in the Alps.

terrain.value: The Alps cover about two-thirds of the country, with the Danube valley and Vienna Basin in the east.

climate.value: Alpine in the mountains and continental elsewhere, with cold, snowy winters and warm summers.

resources.value: Hydropower, forests and timber, some iron ore and salt, and tourism.

disasters.value: Avalanches, landslides and river floods, such as the Danube floods of 2002 and 2013.

disease.value: The country has high-quality public health care, and life expectancy is among the highest in Europe.

migration.value: Guest workers and refugees from the Yugoslav wars; 22.3% of residents were foreign-born in 2024.

economicBase.value: Services, tourism, machinery, steel and chemicals.

tradeRoutes.value: The Danube and Alpine passes link it to Germany, Italy and Eastern Europe; it joined the EU in 1995.

wealth.value: Nominal GDP per person about $67,020 (2026 estimate); living standards are described as high.

governmentType.value: A federal parliamentary republic of nine states, with a president as head of state.

keyRulers.value: Karl Renner was provisional chancellor in 1918 (not first president).

succession.value: Elections to the National Council choose a chancellor, who is head of government.

institutions.value: The National Council and Federal Council, nine federal states (Länder) and an independent constitutional court.

stability.value: Civil war (12–15 February 1934); annexed by Nazi Germany (Anschluss) on 13 March 1938.

eliteConflict.value: Conflict between the Social Democrats and Christian Socials led to civil war in 1934 and the Austrofascist dictatorship.

armyAndTech.value: A small neutral army that does not join military alliances.

majorWars.value: Annexed by Nazi Germany in 1938 and part of it during the Second World War.

territoryChange.value: Lost most of the old empire in 1918; South Tyrol went to Italy and the Sudeten lands to Czechoslovakia.

alliancesRivals.value: State Treaty on 15 May 1955; permanent neutrality declared 26 October 1955; EU member since 1995.

inventions.value: Few major inventions, but Viktor Kaplan’s water turbine (1912) and Sigmund Freud’s psychoanalysis came from Austria.

scienceEducation.value: Public universities with low or no tuition fees, and strong research traditions in physics and medicine.

openness.value: Open to trade and migration; joined the EU in 1995.

communicationTransport.value: Dense railways, Alpine tunnels and motorways that link northern and southern Europe.

religion.value: Catholics were 55.2% of the population in 2021.

languageWriting.value: German is the official language; Hungarian, Slovene and Burgenland Croatian are official regional languages.

artsArchitecture.value: Classical music (Mozart, Haydn, Schubert), Gustav Klimt, Sigmund Freud’s psychoanalysis and Vienna’s Baroque buildings.

socialStructure.value: A large middle class, with a generous welfare state.

sharedIdentity.value: An Austrian identity separate from Germany, mainly after 1945.

dailyLife.value: Apartments and houses; schnitzel, coffee houses.

neighbours.value: Germany, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland.

ideasReligions.value: Permanent neutrality (declared 1955) is a central idea; most people are Roman Catholic.

colonisation.value: Austria itself had no overseas colonies; before 1918 it ruled the Habsburg Empire in Central Europe.

riseSignals.value: German-Austria was declared a democratic republic on 12 November 1918.

peakPeriod.value: Post-war prosperity, from the 1955 State Treaty onward.

declineSignals.value: Annexation by Nazi Germany on 13 March 1938.

outcome.value: Austria continues as an independent republic.
